dimensions.assessment: Affects federal regulators, vehicle manufacturers, automotive aftermarket businesses, dealers, and vehicle owners.
dimensions.evidence: consultation with manufacturers of passenger motor vehicles and equipment, standard settings organizations, the independent automotive aftermarket, and dealers

dimensions.assessment: Establishes formal regulatory guidelines, test protocols, and civil penalties for non-compliance on future model years.
dimensions.evidence: A manufacturer of a passenger motor vehicle or equipment that does not meet the guidelines issued pursuant to this section is subject to the civil penalties

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes contracting authority for independent testing facilities, but does not specify total spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator may contract with independent laboratories and vehicle testing facilities to carry out any testing

dimensions.assessment: Requires new federal agency rulemakings, comprehensive studies, and reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: require the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to establish guidelines for advanced driver assistance systems calibration

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to passenger motor vehicles for model years on and after 2028.
dimensions.evidence: for a model year on and after 2028 maintains functionality

missing_information: Specific funding levels and administrative budgets for conducting the study and testing are absent.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill directs the NHTSA to study and establish guidelines regarding advanced driver assistance systems modifications for vehicles from model year 2028 onward, subjecting non-compliant manufacturers to civil penalties.
